annotation_method: Each base claim and selected probe was independently adjudicated from the complete SYNTHETIC source context before transition comparison.

annotations.text: Treatment B did not reduce mean recovery time in the longitudinal cohort.

evidence.snippet: mean recovery time increased by 0.4 days from baseline rather than decreasing

annotations.rationale: The observed cohort mean moved in the opposite direction, directly supporting non-reduction.

annotations.text: Treatment A had a larger mean recovery-time reduction than placebo in adults.

evidence.snippet: 2.0 days with treatment A and 1.0 day with placebo

annotations.rationale: The descriptive comparison is numeric and does not claim statistical significance.
uncertainty: The between-group difference is not statistically significant.

annotations.text: The treatment A versus placebo recovery-time difference was not statistically significant.

evidence.snippet: The between-group difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.42).

annotations.rationale: The paper directly reports the non-significant comparison.

annotations.text: Baseline exercise was associated with shorter recovery in the observational subgroup.

evidence.snippet: baseline exercise was associated with recovery 0.6 days shorter after adjustment for age

annotations.rationale: The wording stays at the reported associational strength and observational subgroup.
uncertainty: The association must not be interpreted causally.

evidence.snippet: Exactly 12 of 40 SYNTHETIC participants reported improved sleep.

annotations.rationale: Twelve positive cases satisfy the existential claim.

annotations.text: Treatment C reduced mean recovery time in adults with mild symptoms.

evidence.snippet: Among SYNTHETIC adults with mild symptoms, treatment C reduced mean recovery time by 1.1 days relative to placebo.

annotations.rationale: The claim exactly preserves the studied mild-symptom subgroup and comparator.
uncertainty: The result does not cover moderate or severe symptoms.

annotations.text: Treatment B reduced mean recovery time in the longitudinal cohort.

evidence.snippet: mean recovery time increased by 0.4 days from baseline rather than decreasing

annotations.rationale: The observed increase directly contradicts a mean reduction.

annotations.text: Treatment A had a smaller mean recovery-time reduction than placebo in adults.

evidence.snippet: 2.0 days with treatment A and 1.0 day with placebo

annotations.rationale: Two is numerically larger than one, not smaller.

annotations.text: The treatment A versus placebo recovery-time difference was statistically significant.
annotations.rationale: The report directly rejects the asserted significance designation.

annotations.text: Baseline exercise caused shorter recovery in the observational subgroup.

evidence.snippet: Participants were not randomized by exercise exposure, and the study did not identify or estimate a causal effect

annotations.rationale: INITIAL SYNTHETIC ERROR: lack of causal identification was misclassified as affirmative disproof of the causal proposition.
uncertainty: Requires original-source re-review if transition checking flags the verdict.

evidence.snippet: Exactly 12 of 40 SYNTHETIC participants reported improved sleep. The remaining 28 participants did not report improved sleep.

annotations.rationale: The bounded source explicitly provides 28 counterexamples to the universal claim.

annotations.text: Treatment C reduced mean recovery time in adults regardless of symptom severity.

evidence.snippet: The study enrolled no adults with moderate or severe symptoms in this substudy and reported no pooled estimate across all symptom severities.

annotations.rationale: The broader population was not studied or pooled, but that non-reporting does not refute the broader claim.
uncertainty: Effects in moderate/severe groups and all-severity pooled effect are unreported.
